target_customer: Developers of solar, battery storage, EV charging and small data center projects of roughly 1 to 50 MW that need distribution grid interconnection approval
problem: Interconnection applications to distribution utilities are often rejected or delayed because developers cannot see feeder capacity. Developers pick sites blind and re-file.
business_model: B2B software and analysis service sold to project developers (pricing not public)

founders.name: Sara El Baghdadi
founders.background_notes: Grew up in Morocco per the YC page. Best friends with the CTO since middle school.

founders.name: Yassine Guennoun
founders.background_notes: Surname from the company website; the YC page gives only the first name.

competitors.name: Piq Energy
competitors.what: Agentic platform to speed grid interconnection studies

competitors.name: Nira Energy
competitors.what: Software for prospecting grid sites and unclogging interconnection queues

competitors.name: Pearl Street Technologies (Enverus)
competitors.what: Interconnection scenario analysis tool; its site lists it as part of Enverus

technical_complexity.rationale: Replicating feeder level distribution grids and learning what gets projects approved needs power systems modeling and utility data that is fragmented across many utilities. The YC page cites 91 percent approval for sites it modeled in 2025, a company claim.

defensibility.rationale: Models improve with utility specific data and outcomes, which is slow to replicate, but several funded startups attack the same queue problem.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Enverus owns Pearl Street Technologies and sells interconnection products. No incumbent action against Ryhla is recorded as of this research.

market_need_then: Interconnection queues are a widely reported bottleneck for solar, storage and data center projects in 2026, and developers see low approval rates (YC page says 20 to 40 percent typical, company claim).

identity.visual_style: Minimal and text led with a coverage map

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is very new with no press or community evidence found. The spelling is unusual and searches return unrelated names.

outcome_analysis: Ryhla joined YC in Fall 2026 and is active with two founders and no disclosed funding. The founders researched grid intelligence at Stanford, which fits the problem, and interconnection delays are a growing pain. No outcome news exists yet, so the story is too early to judge.
notes: A Nordic9 profile calls Ryhla a Paris based company and says it tracked one investor, but gives no round data; not recorded as a round. No funding press found, so coverage is none_found. Outcome search returned nothing on Ryhla.
